description: Multi-dimensional adversarial review of a diff or capability: correctness, security, and spec compliance, with every finding adversarially verified before it is reported.

findings.title: Removing or moving a Czech hint leaves its translations attached to the wrong hints
findings.evidence: The hint buttons only change `form.hints` (`set({ hints: form.hints.filter((_, k) => k !== i) })`, and `move(form.hints, …)` on lines 273/276). `translations[locale].hints` is never touched. The contract says `Translation.hints` is in the "Same order as the Czech hints" (openapi.yaml:1654), and the UI reads it by position (`tr.hints[i]`, line 353). So after removing hint 1, the old translation of hint 1 is shown and saved as the translation of the old hint 2. Extra trailing entries are also still sent by `toTranslation`.
findings.suggestion: Make every hint add, move and remove apply the same index change to each locale's `translations[l].hints`. The cleanest way is one helper in taskForm.ts (e.g. `removeHint(form, i)` / `moveHint(form, i, d)`) with unit tests.

findings.title: Removing a choice option or a part leaves orphaned or misaligned translation keys that are still sent
findings.evidence: Option keys come from position (`optionKey(j)`), and translations are stored under `"<partKey>.<letter>"`. When option A is removed, B becomes A, but `translations.*.options['p1.B']` keeps the text of the old B. The old `p1.A` text now sits on the option that used to be B. The same happens when a part is removed (`onRemove`, TaskEditorScreen.tsx:208) or a choice part is switched to a non-choice type: its `partLabels` / `options` entries stay in the form, no control renders them, and `nonEmpty()` in `toTranslation` still sends them. If the server refuses unknown keys, the refusal path has no control, so the admin cannot clear it from the UI.
findings.suggestion: When options or parts are removed or re-typed, remap or drop the matching translation entries. Alternatively, in `toTaskInput`, filter `partLabels` and `options` down to the keys of the current parts and options. Add taskForm tests for remove/move/type-change.

findings.title: Non-numeric exactDecimals is silently dropped (NaN serializes to null)
findings.evidence: `exactDecimals: part.type === 'DECIMAL' && part.exactDecimals.trim() ? Number(part.exactDecimals) : null`. For input like "two" or "2,", `Number` returns NaN, and `JSON.stringify` turns NaN into `null`. The server then sees no exact-decimals rule and saves the task without the constraint the admin typed, with no error. The doc comment on `toTaskInput` says values are sent as entered so the server can validate them, which this breaks.
findings.suggestion: Check the field on the client (`/^\d+$/`) and set an error on `parts[i].spec.exactDecimals`. Otherwise, send a value the server will refuse instead of NaN. Never let NaN reach the body. `grade` / `page` go through `Number()` the same way and are worth the same guard.

findings.title: Fast paging starts overlapping pdf.js renders on one canvas; the rejection is unhandled
findings.evidence: `void pdf.data.renderPage(page, canvas.current).then(...)` has no catch. The effect cleanup only sets `current = false` and does not cancel the pdf.js RenderTask. If Next is pressed again before the previous render finishes, pdf.js throws "Cannot use the same canvas during multiple render() operations" (node_modules/pdfjs-dist/build/pdf.mjs:17074). The new page then fails to render, the promise rejects unhandled, and `data-rendered-page` keeps the old page.
findings.suggestion: Have `renderPage` return the RenderTask (or take an AbortSignal) and call `renderTask.cancel()` in the effect cleanup. Catch `RenderingCancelledException` and show `admin.viewer.failed` for any other error.

findings.title: Bulk publish includes selected tasks that the current filters hide
findings.evidence: `selected` is never cleared or narrowed when `filters` change (`apply` only calls setDraft/setErrors/setFilters). After the admin selects tasks and changes a filter, the hidden IDs stay in `selected`. The button still counts them, and `bulkPublish(selected)` publishes tasks the admin can no longer see. Their result rows then show raw UUIDs, because `prompts.get(r.taskId)` only knows the visible list.
findings.suggestion: Either clear `selected` in `apply()`, or publish only `selected.filter(id => list.some(t => t.taskId === id))` and count the same set on the button. Also add a busy flag so publish cannot be submitted twice.

findings.title: useObjectUrl revokes the URL during StrictMode's simulated unmount, then keeps using the revoked URL
findings.evidence: The URL is made in `useMemo` and revoked in an effect cleanup: `useEffect(() => () => (url ? URL.revokeObjectURL(url) : undefined), [url])`. main.tsx renders under `` (React 19). StrictMode runs the cleanup and then re-runs the effect without recomputing the memo, so `` points at a revoked blob URL in development. Creating the URL inside a render-phase memo also leaks when React throws away a render.
findings.suggestion: Create the URL inside the effect and keep it in state: `useEffect(() => { if (!data) return; const u = URL.createObjectURL(data); setUrl(u); return () => URL.revokeObjectURL(u); }, [data])`.

findings.title: Loaded pdf.js documents are cached forever and never destroyed
findings.evidence: `usePdf` stores the opened `PdfDocument` (worker plus a parsed document of up to 50 MB) as query data with `staleTime: Infinity`. Nothing calls `destroy()`. When the query is garbage-collected after `gcTime`, or another source is opened, the pdf.js document and its worker resources stay allocated.
findings.suggestion: Cache only the bytes in the query, and open/destroy the document in a component effect. Alternatively, destroy it via a cache `subscribe` listener on `removed` events.

findings.title: Edits typed while a save is in flight are overwritten
findings.evidence: After `await saveTask(...)`, the create branch calls `setForm(stickyForm(form))` with the `form` captured when submit started, and the update branch calls `setForm(fromAdminTask(saved))`. Only the Save button is disabled while `busy`, so anything the admin types during the request (a likely case in the keyboard-first NFR-8 flow) is silently replaced.
findings.suggestion: Make the fields read-only (e.g. a `<fieldset disabled={busy}>`) during the save. Alternatively, use the functional updater `setForm(f => stickyForm(f))` for the sticky fields and decide explicitly what to keep.

findings.title: Field errors keyed by index stay on the wrong row after parts or hints are reordered or removed
findings.evidence: Server errors are stored by path (`parts[1].spec.accepted[0]`, `hints[2]`) and are only replaced on the next save. Moving or removing a part or hint (`set({ parts: move(form.parts, i, delta) })`) leaves `errors` unchanged. The error and `aria-invalid` then show on whatever item now sits at that index.
findings.suggestion: Clear `errors` (or the affected `parts[`/`hints[` prefixes) whenever a list is restructured.

findings.title: Answer tester keeps stale verdicts after a failed check and drops the server's refusal detail
findings.evidence: In `check`, the `catch { setFailed(true); }` does not clear `results`, so the previous verdicts stay visible next to the 'check failed' alert, as if they belonged to the new answers. The error is also never passed through `fieldErrors`/`problemMessage`, and the Field gets the constant `NO_ERRORS`. A 400 on `answers.<key>` therefore never reaches the field, unlike every other admin form.
findings.suggestion: Call `setResults([])` before or on failure. Keep `fieldErrors(error)` in state and pass it to the Fields, falling back to `problemMessage(error)` the same way TaskEditor does.

findings.title: Picking a PDF file that cannot be read gives an unhandled rejection
findings.evidence: `const check = file ? await checkPdfFile(file) : 'missing';` runs outside the try block, and `submit` is called as `void submit(e)`. `file.slice().arrayBuffer()` rejects with NotReadableError if the file changed or was removed after it was picked. The handler then dies silently with no message. The same applies to `checkImageFile` in ImagesEditor.attach (ImagesEditor.tsx:49).
findings.suggestion: Put the pre-check inside the try, or catch it and show `admin.sources.fileRule` / `admin.images.failed`.

findings.title: Task query key is duplicated as a literal instead of using the private taskKey
findings.evidence: api.ts defines `const taskKey = (taskId) => ['admin', 'task', taskId]` but does not export it. TaskEditorScreen writes `queryClient.setQueryData(['admin', 'task', saved.taskId], saved)` and `invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['admin', 'task', task.taskId] })` (line 390), and both files hard-code `['admin', 'preview', id]`. If one copy of a cache key changes, these silently stop matching.
findings.suggestion: Export `taskKey` and a `previewKey(taskId)` prefix from tasks/api.ts and use them everywhere.

findings.title: Sign-out and idle expiry leave cached admin data (answer specs, PDFs, images) in the QueryClient
findings.evidence: handleSignOut only sets ADMIN_SESSION_KEY to false. The cached admin queries (['admin','task',id] holding answer specs, ['admin','source-file',id] holding the decoded PDF document, and image blobs with staleTime: Infinity, useObjectUrl.ts:9 and PdfViewer.tsx:14) stay in memory. The 401 listener behind idle expiry (adminClient.ts:37) does the same. Suppose the admin signs out on a shared family device and leaves the tab open. Someone at that tab (the child) could read answer keys or workbook pages from the in-memory cache with devtools until the next full page load. The UI never shows them, and every route is a full page load, so the window is small.
findings.suggestion: On sign-out and in the onAdminUnauthorized handler, call queryClient.removeQueries({ queryKey: ['admin'] }) and keep only the session key, or do a full reload to '/admin'. Destroy any open PdfDocument and revoke object URLs (unmounting already revokes them).

findings.title: Checklist coverage: areas reviewed with no exploitable finding
findings.evidence: This entry is informational, not a vulnerability. (1) Authz: every new screen is wrapped in <AdminArea>/<AdminGate> (routes.tsx), but that gate is UI only. All calls go through adminClient under /api/admin/** and nothing here touches child endpoints. Server-side enforcement, IDOR and tenant scoping live in ../backend and are out of scope here. This is a single-admin app, so there are no tenants. The ids from the query string (queryParam) go into openapi-fetch path params, which are URI-encoded, so they can't be used for path traversal. TaskView renders the PartView/TaskView DTO, which has no answer fields, so preview leaks no answer key (FR-27). (2) Auth/CSRF: the CSRF header still comes from the XSRF-TOKEN cookie, and a new test covers the case where the cookie is missing. The test password and CSRF_TOKEN 'xsrf-123' exist only in src/test/fake-admin-backend.ts, and no non-test module imports it, so they stay out of the bundle. (3) Injection: no dangerouslySetInnerHTML or innerHTML. All task, problem and server-message text renders as React text nodes. Hrefs are fixed paths plus server UUIDs. Uploads are checked client-side by magic bytes and size (upload-limits.ts), and the code says the server checks again. PDFs render into a canvas with pdfjs-dist 6.4.299, which is past the CVE-2024-4367 fix in 4.2.67, with the worker same-origin under CSP script-src 'self'. There is no CSV export. (4) Exposure: no compose or CORS changes in this diff. (5) Privacy/IP: the seed data is fictional and self-authored ('Testovací nakladatelství', 'Kolik je 7 + 5?'), PROVENANCE.md is updated, and the recording uses only the fake backend. (6) Secrets: no new VITE_* variables and no .env changes. (7) Dependencies: the new runtime dependency is pdfjs-dist 6.4.299, which pulls in the optional @napi-rs/canvas 1.0.10 (used under Node only). `npm audit` needed approval and was not run, so the dependency check is incomplete, not clean.
findings.suggestion: Run `npm audit` to finish item 7. Confirm the backend's Spring Security matcher for /api/admin/** (including /tasks/{id}/check, /preview, /images and /sources/{id}/file) in the backend review.

findings.title: Ticked task 2.5 (eval case) has no artifact
findings.evidence: tasks.md:11 reads '- [x] 2.5 Eval case for admin copy tone: left planned (evals are SKIP-planned and need a judge this run cannot call).' The diff adds no evals/cases/*.eval.ts file. qa:verify reports 'Overall result: Pass (1 member(s) PLANNED, not yet due: eval-ratchet)' (docs/qa/automated-verification-latest.md:8). findings.title: NFR-8 timed-entry proof only runs against the contract stub; real-stack smoke not run

The explainer says the clip was 'Recorded against the production build (vite preview) with the admin API answered by the contract stub src/test/fake-admin-backend.ts'. tasks.md:22 '[ ] 4.4 Smoke against the compose stack … NOT RUN in this change, the running stack has no slice 5 backend'. findings.title: Store scenario 'Preview matches the child task screen' (pixel/text parity) deferred and missing from the delta
findings.evidence: The store requires an e2e test comparing the admin preview task area with the child task screen ('accessible text content … identical' and '≤ 1 % of pixels'). The delta 'Preview and answer tester screen' requirement leaves this scenario out. Only design.md:37 records the deferral ('pixel comparison needs the child screen (slice 7)'). Neither tasks.md nor the proposal has a follow-up item, so nothing keeps it from being silently forgotten. The current mechanism is only that TaskView.tsx is shared.

findings.title: Undocumented drift: image removal (deleteTaskImage) in the editor
findings.evidence: The delta requirement 'Task images in the editor' says the editor SHALL 'attach PNG or JPG images, refuse other types … show server refusals, and move an image earlier or later (reorderTaskImages)'. Removal is not mentioned. The code adds `<Button … onClick={() => void run(() => deleteImage(task.taskId, imageId), null)}>` and api.ts:56 calls DELETE /api/admin/tasks/{taskId}/images/{imageId}. That endpoint exists in openapi.yaml:683 (deleteTaskImage), so the contract is fine, but no spec requirement backs the behaviour.
findings.suggestion: Amend the delta requirement to include 'remove an image (deleteTaskImage)', with a scenario. The unit test 'attaches a PNG, moves it first and removes the other' already exists.

findings.title: Bulk publish selection survives filter changes, so hidden tasks can be published
findings.evidence: Spec: 'publish 1 to 100 selected tasks in one step, listing the result of each'. `apply()` (lines 136-141) changes `filters` but never resets `selected`. Rows that drop out of the filtered list stay selected and are sent by `bulkPublish(selected)` (line 153). The only cue is the count in 'Publish selected (N)'.
findings.suggestion: Clear the selection (or intersect it with the visible list) when filters change, and add a unit test. Alternatively, amend the spec if publishing a selection that spans filters is intended.

findings.title: Bulk publish result falls back to raw task UUIDs when the list is filtered by DRAFT
findings.evidence: `const prompts = new Map(list.map(...))` is recomputed from the refetched list after `invalidateQueries(TASKS_KEY)` (line 156). With status=DRAFT active, the most common publish workflow, the newly published tasks leave `list`, and line 253 renders `prompts.get(r.taskId) ?? r.taskId`, which is a UUID. The spec says the result SHALL 'list every task with whether it is now PUBLISHED'. The tasks are listed, but they cannot be identified by the admin.
findings.suggestion: Snapshot the prompt excerpts of the selected tasks before calling bulkPublish and use that snapshot to label the results. Add a test for 'DRAFT filter → publish → results named by prompt'.

findings.title: Answer tester renders CHOICE_SINGLE parts as checkboxes
findings.evidence: `if (part.options) { … <input type="checkbox" …` is used for every choice part, so the admin can tick several options on a single-choice part. The child TaskView uses radios for CHOICE_SINGLE (TaskView.tsx:54). Spec FR-10: the tester shows 'per part, the checker's verdict'. The contract accepts arrays, so this does not break the API, but the tester behaves unlike the child UI it is meant to mirror.
findings.suggestion: Use radio inputs for CHOICE_SINGLE in the tester, matching TaskView. Add a unit test.

findings.title: Preview translation toggle only reaches the first configured task locale
findings.evidence: `onToggleTranslation={() => setLocale(locale === null ? firstLocale : null)}` with `firstLocale = reference.data.taskLocales[0]`. The editor offers every configured locale ('New locale by configuration only', TaskEditorScreen.tsx:296), but the preview can never show the translation of a second locale. The delta only requires 'the translation toggle', so this is a gap, not a contradiction, once a second locale is configured.
findings.suggestion: Add a locale choice next to the toggle when taskLocales.length > 1, or record in the spec that the preview shows only the primary secondary locale.

findings.title: Inverted button styles: disabled 'Move part' buttons look like buttons, the enabled 'Remove part 1' looks like plain text
findings.evidence: In the Part 1 action row, 'Move part 1 up' and 'Move part 1 down' are disabled (PartEditor.tsx:194/197, index 0 = count-1) but show a filled grey pill. 'Remove part 1', which is enabled (PartEditor.tsx:200, no disabled prop), shows as bare bold text with no border or fill. So the enabled control looks inert and the disabled ones look clickable. The same ghost variant is used for 'Remove option' and 'Remove accepted answer'.
findings.suggestion: Give enabled ghost buttons a visible button style (outline or underline plus a hover/focus state), and make disabled ones look clearly muted with no pill fill. Check the ghost variant's rules in the design system rather than patching locally. Also consider disabling 'Remove part' when it is the only part (count === 1), so it matches the move buttons and a task can't be left with zero parts.

findings.title: Still is taken after the form reset, so it shows a blank form under a 'Task saved as draft' banner
findings.evidence: The clip claims NFR-8/FR-3 single-part entry (prompt, topic, task number, expected value). In the still, Prompt, Task number and Accepted answer 1 are all empty, and only the green 'Task saved as draft.' panel shows a save happened. None of the typed content is visible, so a reviewer can't confirm from the image what was entered or saved.
findings.suggestion: Take the still just before Enter, with the fields filled in. Or take a second still and show the saved values, e.g. the task list row or the 'Edit saved task' view, so the evidence image shows what the clip proves.

findings.title: Save confirmation and Images panel are out of order around the Save button
findings.evidence: The 'Task saved as draft' panel sits above 'Save task', and the 'Images' card comes after the Save button. So the main action is in the middle of the form instead of at the end, and the status message comes before the action it reports on.
findings.suggestion: Put Images above the Save action, or make the action bar sticky at the bottom. Show the save status next to or after the Save button, as a live region.

findings.title: Helper text above the form may fall below AA contrast
findings.evidence: The light-grey helper 'Enter in a single-line field, or Ctrl+Enter anywhere, saves the task.' on the cream background is much fainter than the field labels. This is the only on-screen hint for the keyboard save shortcut.
findings.suggestion: Measure the contrast of the muted text token against the cream surface (it needs ≥ 4.5:1). If it fails, use a darker design-system text token.

result.reasoning:
The finding holds. The bug is real and I couldn't refute it.

- **The buttons only touch the Czech hints.** At `TaskEditorScreen.tsx:273`, `:276` and `:279`, the move and remove buttons call `set({ hints: ... })`. `set` (line 69) is a plain shallow merge, `setForm(f => ({...f, ...patch}))`, so `translations` is left as it was. Nothing else syncs `translations[locale].hints`.
- **Translations are matched by position.** The UI reads a translated hint as `tr.hints[i]` (line 353). Typing in a translation field rebuilds the array by position from `form.hints` (line 355).
- **What goes wrong.** Say Czech hints are [h1, h2] and the Ukrainian ones are [t1, t2]. Remove h1 and the form now shows h2 next to t1. On save, `toTranslation` (`taskForm.ts:132`) maps the whole `tr.hints` array, so it sends [t1, t2] against a single Czech hint. That pairs t1 with h2 and leaves an extra trailing entry, exactly as the finding says. Moving a hint misaligns them the same way.
- **The tests don't cover it.** The test at `TaskEditorScreen.test.tsx:312` checks reordering only with no translations present.

Severity "major" is fair: a quiet editing action saves wrong translations into the content.

The finding is confirmed. `set` (line 69) is a plain shallow merge, `({ ...f, ...patch })`, so it never touches `translations`. The remove button (line 279) and the move-up/move-down buttons (lines 273 and 276) only rewrite `form.hints`. Translated hints are read by position: `tr.hints[i]` on line 353, with the label/path `hints[${i}]`.

Here is how it happens. An admin edits a task that has Czech hints [A, B] and English translations [a, b], then removes hint A. The Czech list becomes [B], but the English list stays [a, b]. The UI now shows "a" as the English translation of B. `toTranslation` (taskForm.ts:132) maps every entry of `tr.hints` and only trims trailing nulls. So the save sends hints [a, b] against Czech [B]: the translation is wrong, and there is an extra entry. Moving a hint swaps the Czech order but not the translations, so they no longer match.

Nothing else catches this: no effect or helper in taskForm syncs the arrays. Any admin who edits a translated task can hit it with ordinary clicks. The result is wrong hint text shown to the child, or the backend rejecting the save if it checks the counts match. Major severity is appropriate.

The mechanism is real. I checked it in the code:

- **Option removal shifts the translations.** `PartEditor.tsx:110` removes an option by filtering it out of the array. Option keys come only from position (`optionKey(i)` in `taskForm.ts:63`, used in `toSpec`, line 124).
- **Translation keys are positional too.** Option translations are stored in `TranslationForm.options` under `${part.key}.${optionKey(j)}` (`TaskEditorScreen.tsx:324`). Nothing remaps them when an option is removed.
- **Result:** removing option A turns the old B into the new A. Its translation input then reads `tr.options['p1.A']`, which still holds the old A's translated text. The child would see a translated option that doesn't match the Czech one.
- **The last key is orphaned.** The last key (e.g. `p1.C`) stays in the form and no control renders it any more.
- **Parts leave orphans too.** Part keys are stable (`newPart`), so removing a part (`TaskEditorScreen.tsx:208`) or changing its type away from choice leaves `partLabels[p.key]` and `options['p.key.*']` entries with no control.
- **The orphans are sent.** `toTranslation` (lines 128–139) sends every non-empty entry through `nonEmpty()`, with no filtering against the current parts or options. So orphaned entries go to the server.

Nothing in the form guards against any of this. The one uncertain part is whether the server rejects unknown keys. Even if it accepts them, the misaligned option translation is a real correctness bug that silently corrupts content. Keep the severity at major.

I could not refute this. The code confirms the mechanism, and a normal admin can trigger it with a few clicks.

**Option removal.** `PartEditor.tsx:110` just filters `part.options` by position. Option keys are recomputed from position with `optionKey(i)`, in `taskForm.ts:63` and `:124`. Translations live in `form.translations[locale].options`, keyed by `"<partKey>.<letter>"` (`TaskEditorScreen.tsx:323-338`). Nothing remaps or prunes them when an option is removed.

Example: a part has options A/B/C with translations p1.A, p1.B and p1.C, and the admin removes A.
- Old B is now A, but it still shows and saves the p1.A translation, which belongs to the deleted option.
- p1.B, the old C, now carries the text that was written for old B.
- p1.C still holds old C's text, but no control renders it.
- `toTranslation` sends every non-empty entry (`nonEmpty`, `taskForm.ts:128-135`), so the orphaned p1.C is still sent.

**Part removal and type change.** Part removal (`TaskEditorScreen.tsx:208`) only filters `form.parts`. `partLabels[key]` and the `options` entries for that part remain and are sent. Switching a part to a non-choice type hides the option translation inputs (they only render for choice parts), but `tr.options` keeps its entries and they are still sent.

Visibility differs. The misaligned translations do show up in the translation inputs, so an attentive admin could notice them. The orphaned keys never render, so the admin cannot see or clear them from the UI.

I did not check whether the server rejects unknown keys. That part of the claim is conditional. Even without it, the misalignment is a real correctness bug: a translated option text gets attached to the wrong option and may reach the child. I'm keeping the severity at major.

Confirmed. At taskForm.ts:114, `exactDecimals` becomes `Number(part.exactDecimals)` whenever the type is DECIMAL and the trimmed string is not empty. The input that feeds it (PartEditor.tsx:171) is a plain text `<input inputMode="numeric">`, not `type="number"`. So the browser lets values like "two" or "2," through unchanged, and `Number()` turns them into NaN. Before `toTaskInput`, `save()` in TaskEditorScreen.tsx:73-83 checks only `sourceRef.page` (with `parsePage`, and only when a source is selected). Nothing checks `exactDecimals`. The body is sent as JSON, where NaN becomes `null`, so the server gets "no exact-decimals rule", which is a valid value. It saves without error, and no field error is shown. This also contradicts the doc comment at line 142 ("Values are sent as entered; the server validates them"). It is somewhat visible after the fact: on update, `fromAdminTask(saved)` shows the field as empty, and on create the form resets. Either way the admin gets no error, and the constraint they typed is silently lost. On the side note: `grade` comes from a `<select>`, so it is safe. `page` is guarded when a source is set. So the main claim stands, but the grade/page part of the suggestion is weaker. Keeping severity at major, since this silently changes how answers are graded for authored content.

I confirmed the bug and can reproduce it.

1. **The field accepts any text.** `src/features/tasks/PartEditor.tsx:171` renders exactDecimals as a plain `<input>` with only `inputMode="numeric"`. That attribute only suggests a soft keyboard.
